- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to counteract pessimism.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day forecast when sentiment is neutral or mixed — apply downward correction of 2–5% for first 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 1–3% upward bias to offset.
- Sentiment volatility >0.5 in last 3 days → model overreacts → reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 5 days.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model is lagging — apply 1–3% upward correction for next 3 days.
